Il petrolio è in calo, ma la guerra tra Israele e Iran continua a pesare sui mercati. L'S&P 500 è in rialzo, ma il Fear & Greed Index è a 21, in territorio di Extreme Fear.

Oil is down, but the Israel-Iran war continues to weigh on markets. S&P 500 is up, but the Fear & Greed Index is at 21, in Extreme Fear territory.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la giornata con un tono positivo. Il Nikkei giapponese ha guadagnato il 2.4% a 57,877, mentre lo Shanghai cinese ha registrato un aumento dello 0.9% a 4,000. Anche l'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha mostrato un incremento dello 0.9% a 25,881. Questi dati potrebbero anticipare un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

La giornata odierna sembra caratterizzata da un sentiment di risk-off. L'S&P 500 ha chiuso con un guadagno dell'1% a 6,900, mentre il VIX, indice della paura, ha sceso del 2% a 19. Il Dollar Index (DXY) ha registrato una lieve flessione dello 0.1% a 98. I tassi di interesse sono stati oggetto di attenzione: il tasso decennale USA è sceso dello 0.5% a 4.3%, e il TLT Bond USA 20Y ha guadagnato lo 0.3% a 87. L'oro, bene rifugio per eccellenza, ha guadagnato l'1.3% a $4,800 l'oncia.

Sul fronte geopolitico, la situazione nel Medio Oriente resta tesa. Le esportazioni cinesi hanno subito un rallentamento a causa dei disordini nella regione. La possibile chiusura dello Stretto di Hormuz, cruciale per il trasporto del petrolio, potrebbe scatenare una crisi globale di sicurezza alimentare. Gli Stati Uniti hanno annunciato un blocco navale dello Stretto di Hormuz dopo il fallimento dei colloqui di pace con l'Iran. Questi eventi hanno avuto un impatto sui prezzi delle materie prime, con il Brent che ha perso lo 0.9% a $98.

Sul fronte macroeconomico, l'attenzione si concentra sui dati in arrivo. Negli USA, il prossimo dato importante sarà il PIL del primo trimestre, in uscita il 29 aprile. La BCE ha recentemente mantenuto i tassi di interesse invariati, con il tasso dei depositi al 2%. La liquidità globale, misurata dal Global M2, continua ad espandersi, con un aumento del 4.9% su base annua a $23T. Questi fattori influenzeranno sicuramente le decisioni future delle banche centrali.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 

Iniziamo il nostro deep dive con Bitcoin. La recente performance di prezzo ha visto BTC raggiungere i 74.582 dollari, con un incremento del 5.4%. Sul fronte degli ETF, registriamo un afflusso giornaliero netto di 257 milioni di dollari, segno di un interesse istituzionale ancora molto presente. Tecnicamente, il trend di breve termine sembra orientato al rialzo, ma permane una certa volatilità.

Passando alle altcoin, Ethereum ha mostrato un'impennata notevole, raggiungendo i 2.379 dollari con un +8.9%. Solana e Binance Coin hanno anch'esse registrato aumenti, rispettivamente del 4.7% a 86 dollari e del 3.4% a 616 dollari. Questi movimenti suggeriscono una ripresa generale del mercato crypto.

Per quanto riguarda il sentiment, l'indice Fear & Greed è sceso a 21, in territorio di Extreme Fear. Questo livello indica che gli investitori sono estremamente cauti, il che potrebbe preludere a un rimbalzo del mercato. La correlazione con i dati macroeconomici, come l'inflazione e i tassi di interesse, resta una variabile importante da monitorare.

In sintesi, il mercato crypto sembra essere in una fase di recupero, con Bitcoin e le principali altcoin che mostrano segnali positivi. Tuttavia, permane una certa incertezza legata ai dati macroeconomici e alle dinamiche geopolitiche, come evidenziato dalle notizie relative all'interesse dell'Iran per Bitcoin e agli sforzi dell'ECB per tokenizzare i mercati dei capitali europei.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati asiatici e le notizie economiche in uscita. Un saluto da Prais Alért, arrivederci alla prossima puntata.
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global sentiment is cautious, with a risk-off mood prevailing in the markets. This is reflected in the slight declines in equities and the strengthening of safe-haven assets.

In traditional markets, equities are showing a mixed picture. At the last close, the S&P 500 was up 1% to 6900, while the STOXX 600 gained 0.8% to 62. The NIKKEI closed up 2.4% to 57,877. In the currency markets, the EUR/USD pair is trading at 1.2, up 0.9% on the day. The Dollar Index (DXY) is down 0.1% to 98. Commodities are seeing some movement, with GOLD up 1.3% to $4800/oz and BRENT down 0.9% to $98. Bond markets are seeing some buying, with the TLT Bond USA 20Y up 0.3% to 87 and the US 10Y Yield down 0.5% to 4.3%.

Geopolitically, tensions in the Middle East are escalating, with China's exports slowing down due to the turmoil. There are concerns about a potential global food security crisis if the Strait of Hormuz is closed. In economic news, Singapore has tightened its monetary policy due to the energy shock hitting Asia. The digital euro project is also being implemented. Inflation and interest rates are being closely watched, with China's export growth slowing down due to the Iran war pushing up import bills.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. 
    Starting with Bitcoin, we see a price increase of 5.4% to $74,582. The recent BTC ETF daily net inflow of $257M indicates growing institutional interest. Despite this, Bitcoin's struggle to build a long-lasting uptrend continues. 

    Moving on to altcoins, we observe significant gains in ETH, SOL, and BNB. ETH is up 8.9% to $2,379, SOL is up 4.7% to $86, and BNB is up 3.4% to $616. The overall crypto market seems to be experiencing a resurgence, with crypto ETPs seeing $1.1B inflows, marking the strongest gains since January.

    In terms of sentiment, the Fear & Greed Index is at 21, indicating extreme fear. This could potentially signal a buying opportunity, but it's essential to consider various factors before making any investment decisions. The ECB is also exploring tokenized EU capital markets with strict guardrails, and there's been news of Capital B expanding its treasury to 2,925 BTC. 
    That's all for today's crypto update.

Thanks for tuning in. We'll be back tomorrow with more market insights. Keep an eye on the key events and data releases that could impact your trades. Until then, stay informed and stay ahead. A final word from Prais Alért - see you tomorrow. Have a great day!

articles.title: A Closed Strait of Hormuz Risks a Global Food Security Crisis
articles.snippet: The war in Iran has done more than rattle energy markets. It has exposed an ordinary farm input as a strategic commodity. Urea is a concentrated, easy-to-transport nitrogen fertilizer that increases the yields of many crops, especially staple grains like corn, rice, and wheat. These small white pellets are essentially natural gas in solid form, bound with nitrogen fixed from the atmosphere through the energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process. They are literally a building block of the Green Revolution and critical to global food security.While the recent U.S.-Iranian ceasefire may have paused or limited hostilities, it already shows signs of breaking apart, The post A Closed Strait of Hormuz Risks a Global Food Security Crisis appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Implementing the digital euro project
articles.snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) is working on a digital version of the euro, a project started back in 2020 that is coming closer to fruition as the enabling EU legislation progresses. The ECB has designed a digital equivalent of cash, aimed at complementing physical euros for day-to-day payments. Its approach may be compared and contrasted with the US Federal Reserve’s reluctance to introduce a digital dollar and with the People’s Bank of China’s definition of the digital yuan largely as a bank deposit. articles.title: The Bromine Chokepoint: How Strife in the Middle East Could Halt Production of the World’s Memory Chips
articles.snippet: The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in an unstable ceasefire, has exposed a structural failure in the global semiconductor memory supply chain, and it is not the one analysts seem to be tracking. The story receiving attention is helium: Qatar’s Ras Laffan facility went offline, a 45-day inventory clock started running, and spot prices doubled within days. The story receiving almost no attention is bromine, and it is potentially the more dangerous one. Structural theories of power transition would lead us to expect sharper and earlier confrontation as capabilities converged. Instead, the U.S.-Chinese rivalry deepened gradually, punctuated by crises but rarely exploding into decisive pushback. articles.title: Why Iran Wants Bitcoin For Safe Passage Though The Strait Of Hormuz
articles.snippet: Bitcoin Magazine Why Iran Wants Bitcoin For Safe Passage Though The Strait Of Hormuz Iran is demanding that oil tankers pay a $1-per-barrel toll in Bitcoin to pass safely through the Strait of Hormuz during the current two-week ceasefire with the United States, according to a Financial Times report citing Iranian oil exporters’ union spokesman Hamid Hosseini. The move allows Tehran to monetize its control over the chokepoint — which handles 20% of global oil flows — while bypassing U.S. sanctions that block traditional payment rails. Unlike dollars, yuan or gold, Bitcoin offers neutral, censorship-resistant settlement that cannot be traced or confiscated, validating long-standing Bitcoiner predictions that it functions as sovereign money for sanctioned nations. This post Why Iran Wants Bit

articles.title: Trump Signals High Gas Prices Through November Midterms
articles.snippet: U.S. President Donald Trump has acknowledged that gasoline prices might remain high through the November 2026 midterm elections, a rare admission of the potential political fallout from the ongoing war in the Middle East. Trump told Fox News' Maria Bartiromo that gas prices could "stay the same, or maybe a little bit higher, but it should be around the same" when asked if gas prices would be lower by the fall. Trump has defended the surge as a "very small price to pay" for long-term global safety and the neutralization of Iran's nuclear threat.…
